column3: THE SMALL BOAT RESTED BESIDE THE RIVER. A COOL WIND MOVED THROUGH THE TREES. WE PACKED OUR BAGS BEFORE THE SUN CAME UP AND WALKED ALONG THE QUIET BANK. THERE WAS NO HURRY. THE WATER CARRIED THE FIRST LIGHT PAST THE OLD WOODEN BRIDGE.

A LETTER ARRIVED AT THE HOUSE THIS MORNING. IT CAME FROM A FRIEND WHO LIVES BEYOND THE HILLS. SHE WROTE ABOUT HER GARDEN AND THE BIRDS THAT VISIT IT. WE WILL WRITE BACK AFTER DINNER AND TELL HER ABOUT OUR OWN NEW PLANS.

THE WORKSHOP WAS WARM AND BRIGHT. TOOLS HUNG IN NEAT ROWS ABOVE THE TABLE. EACH PIECE OF WOOD HAD A DIFFERENT GRAIN AND A DIFFERENT PURPOSE. WE MEASURED TWICE BEFORE MAKING THE FIRST CUT. BY EVENING THE LITTLE SHELF WAS READY FOR ITS FINAL COAT.

THE MARKET OPENS EARLY ON SATURDAY. PEOPLE BRING FRUIT AND FLOWERS FROM THE NEARBY FARMS. THE BAKER SELLS ROUND LOAVES STILL WARM FROM THE OVEN. WE ALWAYS TAKE A BASKET AND WALK HOME BY THE LONG ROAD THROUGH THE PARK.

A SOFT RAIN BEGAN WHILE WE WERE READING. THE WINDOW WAS OPEN JUST ENOUGH TO HEAR THE DROPS. SOMEWHERE DOWN THE STREET A DOOR CLOSED. THE ROOM GREW DARKER BUT THE LAMP MADE A SMALL CIRCLE OF LIGHT ON THE PAGE.

THE TRAIN LEFT THE STATION ON TIME. FIELDS GAVE WAY TO STONE WALLS AND LOW HOUSES. AT THE NEXT STOP A CHILD WAVED FROM THE PLATFORM. WE WATCHED THE LANDSCAPE CHANGE AND SHARED THE LUNCH WE HAD MADE BEFORE LEAVING HOME.

AT THE END OF THE NARROW LANE STOOD A WEATHER STATION THAT HAD BEEN CLOSED FOR MANY YEARS. ITS WINDOWS WERE CLEAN BUT THE SIGN ABOVE THE DOOR HAD FADED IN THE SUN. A RETIRED TEACHER HAD ASKED FOR PERMISSION TO TURN THE BUILDING INTO A PLACE WHERE CHILDREN COULD STUDY THE SKY. ON THE FIRST OPEN DAY SHE SET THREE EMPTY JARS ON A BENCH AND INVITED EVERY VISITOR TO GUESS WHICH WOULD COLLECT THE MOST RAIN. THE ANSWERS WERE WRITTEN IN A BLUE NOTEBOOK. SOME CHILDREN STUDIED THE ROOF BEFORE THEY CHOSE. OTHERS WANTED TO KNOW HOW STRONG THE WIND WOULD BE. BY THE END OF THE AFTERNOON EVERYONE HAD A DIFFERENT THEORY. THE TEACHER DID NOT GIVE THEM THE RIGHT ANSWER. SHE ASKED THEM TO COME BACK NEXT WEEK WITH SOMETHING THEY HAD NOTICED ABOUT THE WEATHER AT HOME. A QUIET BOY AT THE BACK SUGGESTED ADDING A FOURTH JAR UNDER THE TREE. THAT IDEA LED TO A LONG DISCUSSION ABOUT FAIR TESTS. WHEN THE DOORS FINALLY CLOSED THERE WERE WET FOOTPRINTS ON THE FLOOR AND MANY MORE QUESTIONS IN THE NOTEBOOK THAN THERE HAD BEEN IN THE MORNING.

THE MAPMAKER HAD NEVER VISITED THE ISLAND. ALL HE KNEW OF IT CAME FROM THE STORIES OF PEOPLE WHO HAD SAILED PAST ITS SHORES. ONE CAPTAIN DESCRIBED A TALL RED CLIFF WHILE ANOTHER INSISTED THAT THE WHOLE COAST WAS FLAT. RATHER THAN CHOOSE BETWEEN THEM THE MAPMAKER DREW TWO SMALL SKETCHES IN THE MARGIN AND LEFT THE MAIN OUTLINE UNFINISHED. MONTHS LATER A FISHER ARRIVED WITH A DRAWING MADE FROM THE EASTERN BAY. IT SHOWED THAT BOTH CAPTAINS HAD BEEN RIGHT. THE CLIFF STOOD ON THE FAR SIDE OF A LONG LOW HEADLAND. THE MAPMAKER ADDED THIS DETAIL AND SENT A COPY TO EACH OF THEM. IN HIS LETTER HE EXPLAINED THAT A GOOD MAP WAS NOT A COLLECTION OF CONFIDENT GUESSES. IT WAS A RECORD OF WHAT HAD BEEN SEEN AND WHAT STILL NEEDED TO BE CHECKED. HE KEPT THE ORIGINAL MARGINAL SKETCHES EVEN AFTER THE COASTLINE WAS COMPLETE. THEY REMINDED HIM THAT TWO HONEST OBSERVERS COULD RETURN WITH VERY DIFFERENT DESCRIPTIONS. HIS NEXT MAP INCLUDED A LIST OF THE DIRECTIONS FROM WHICH EACH IMPORTANT LANDMARK HAD BEEN OBSERVED.

EVERY AUTUMN THE COMMUNITY HALL HOSTED A REPAIR AFTERNOON. PEOPLE BROUGHT BROKEN CHAIRS LOOSE BUTTONS AND LAMPS THAT NO LONGER WORKED. THE VOLUNTEERS DID NOT PROMISE THAT EVERYTHING COULD BE FIXED. INSTEAD THEY PROMISED TO LOOK CAREFULLY AND EXPLAIN WHAT THEY FOUND. ONE WOMAN ARRIVED WITH A MUSIC BOX THAT HAD BELONGED TO HER GRANDFATHER. IT PLAYED THREE NOTES AND THEN STOPPED. A YOUNG VOLUNTEER ASKED HER TO TURN THE HANDLE SLOWLY WHILE HE LISTENED. HE THOUGHT THE TROUBLE MIGHT BE A BENT PART BUT DID NOT OPEN THE CASE UNTIL HE HAD DRAWN A DIAGRAM OF ITS OUTSIDE. WORKING TOGETHER THEY DISCOVERED A SMALL GRAIN OF SAND CAUGHT NEAR THE WHEEL. AFTER IT WAS REMOVED THE TUNE RETURNED. THE WOMAN STAYED TO HELP SOMEONE ELSE SEW A PATCH ON A COAT. BY CLOSING TIME THE HALL WAS FULL OF CONVERSATION AND THE SMELL OF TEA. NOT EVERY OBJECT HAD BEEN REPAIRED BUT EVERY OWNER LEFT WITH A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IT WORKED. THE VOLUNTEERS AGREED THAT THIS WAS ALSO A USEFUL KIND OF SUCCESS.

THE NEW LIBRARIAN FOUND A BOX OF UNLABELED PHOTOGRAPHS IN THE STORE ROOM. MOST SHOWED ORDINARY STREETS AND BUILDINGS BUT NOBODY KNEW WHEN THEY HAD BEEN TAKEN. SHE PUT ONE PICTURE ON THE NOTICE BOARD EACH WEEK AND ASKED VISITORS WHAT THEY RECOGNIZED. AN OLDER RESIDENT IDENTIFIED A SHOP THAT HAD CLOSED BEFORE THE BRIDGE WAS BUILT. A STUDENT NOTICED THE SHAPE OF A BUS IN THE BACKGROUND. ANOTHER VISITOR REMEMBERED THE TREE OUTSIDE THE POST OFFICE AND BROUGHT A FAMILY ALBUM TO COMPARE. LITTLE BY LITTLE THE DATES BECAME CLEARER. THE LIBRARIAN WROTE DOWN EACH CLUE WITH THE NAME OF THE PERSON WHO PROVIDED IT. WHEN TWO MEMORIES DISAGREED SHE KEPT BOTH UNTIL ANOTHER PICTURE HELPED RESOLVE THE QUESTION. THE FINISHED DISPLAY DID MORE THAN SHOW THE TOWN AS IT HAD ONCE BEEN. IT SHOWED HOW MANY SMALL PIECES OF KNOWLEDGE COULD FIT TOGETHER. ON THE LAST DAY A CHILD ASKED WHETHER PEOPLE IN THE FUTURE WOULD KNOW WHEN THEIR OWN PICTURES HAD BEEN TAKEN. THE LIBRARIAN HANDED HIM A PENCIL AND A SHEET OF LABELS.

BEFORE DAWN THE WALKERS GATHERED AT THE FOOT OF THE RIDGE. EACH CARRIED WATER A SMALL MEAL AND A LIGHT JACKET. THEIR GUIDE EXPLAINED THAT THE SHORTEST PATH WAS NOT ALWAYS THE BEST ONE AFTER RAIN. THEY TOOK THE LONGER TRAIL THROUGH THE PINES WHERE THE GROUND WAS FIRM AND THE SLOPE WAS GENTLE. HALF WAY UP THEY STOPPED TO WATCH A PAIR OF BIRDS CIRCLE ABOVE THE VALLEY. ONE WALKER WAS EAGER TO CONTINUE BUT THE GUIDE POINTED OUT THAT THE CLOUDS WERE MOVING FASTER THAN EXPECTED. THEY CHECKED THE MAP AND CHOSE A SHELTERED PLACE FOR THEIR BREAK. THE SUMMIT COULD WAIT UNTIL THE WEATHER WAS CLEAR. DURING THE REST THEY COMPARED THE SOUNDS THEY HAD HEARD ALONG THE TRAIL. THERE HAD BEEN RUNNING WATER A DISTANT BELL AND THE SOFT CREAK OF BRANCHES. WHEN THEY STARTED DOWN AGAIN THE YOUNGEST WALKER NOTICED A SIGN THAT EVERYONE HAD MISSED ON THE WAY UP. IT MARKED AN OLD ORCHARD JUST BEYOND THE TREES. THEY DECIDED TO RETURN ON ANOTHER DAY WITH MORE TIME AND BETTER WEATHER.
